Consider the following PR description:
Admin doesn't display properly unicode chars in JSONFields.
Description
	 
		(last modified by ZhaoQi99)
	 
>>> import json
>>> print json.dumps('中国')
"\u4e2d\u56fd"
json.dumps use ASCII encoding by default when serializing Chinese.
So when we edit a JsonField which contains Chinese character in Django admin,it will appear in ASCII characters.
I have try to fix this this problem in ​https://github.com/adamchainz/django-mysql/pull/714.And it works prefectly.

I can see the issue clearly now. The `prepare_value` method at line 1261 uses `json.dumps(value, cls=self.encoder)` without `ensure_ascii=False`. This method is responsible for converting the Python value to a JSON string for display in the form.

I need to change line 1261 from:
```python
return json.dumps(value, cls=self.encoder)
```
to:
```python
return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, cls=self.encoder)
```

The `has_changed` method (lines 1269-1270) also uses `json.dumps`, but those are just for comparison purposes and don't affect display, so they don't need to be changed. The `ensure_ascii` setting doesn't affect the data structure or comparison, just how the string is displayed.
